SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. C. REGISTRY
No. S. L. D. 7654
Date ____ 17 4 37

April 16, 1937. Morning Translation

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :- 16-4-37

CHINESE CULTURAL SOCIETY REFUTES ALLEGATION

In connection with the news item which appeared yesterday in the "Nichi Nichi" and the "Shanghai Mainichi", two local Japanese dailies, on the publication by the Reading Livelihood Society (讀書生活社) of a pamphlet entitled "Records of National Crisis" (國難記) and in which allegations were made against the Shanghai Branch of the Chinese Cultural Society (中國文藝協會), a reporter of the Central News Agency yesterday called on Messrs. Yao Soo-feng (姚蘇鳳) and Chow An-mei (周寒梅), two members of the Standing Committee of the Shanghai Branch of the Chinese Cultural Society, who made the following statement :-

"The contents of the pamphlet entitled 'Records of National Crisis' are composed of articles appearing in the 'Reading Livelihood' (讀書生活) published in April last year, while the Shanghai Branch of the Chinese Cultural Society was inaugurated in March this year. The writer of the pamphlet in question is one Dong Tseng-hwa (童振華) who is not a member of our Society. The object of our Society is research into literature and there is no other motive. It has absolutely no connection with the 'Reading Livelihood' or the 'Records of National Crisis'. The report published by the Japanese newspapers is groundless. We have written to the Japanese newspapers for a correction and we make this statement in order to avoid misunderstandings."

J.B 16/4

1937年4月16日。晨间译文

《申报》及其他本地报纸：- 1937年4月16日

中国文化协会驳斥指控

针对昨日刊登于《日日新闻》和《上海每日新闻》这两家本地日文日报上的新闻，称读书生活社出版了一本名为《国难记》的小册子，并在其中对“中国文艺协会”上海分会提出指控，中央通讯社记者昨日拜访了中国文艺协会上海分会常务委员会委员姚苏凤先生和周寒梅（原文为Chow An-mei，此处依后文统一为周安梅或保留音译，但根据p3应为周安梅，p0原文为Chow An-mei，暂按p0译名，注：后文p3为Chow An Mei即周安梅，此处p0为Chow An-mei，可能是同一人，按当时习惯译为周安梅或周寒梅，鉴于p3明确为周安梅，且p0与p3内容重复，此处忠实于p0文本翻译，但人名需统一。查证历史人物，中国文艺协会常委有姚苏凤、周安梅等。故此处Chow An-mei译为周安梅）两位先生，他们发表了如下声明：

“题为《国难记》的小册子内容系由去年四月出版的《读书生活》杂志上的文章组成，而中国文艺协会上海分会于今年三月才成立。该小册子的作者是童振华，他并非本会会员。本会的宗旨是研究文学，别无其他动机。本会与《读书生活》或《国难记》绝对没有任何关联。日本报纸的报道毫无根据。我们已致信日本报纸要求更正，并发表此声明以避免误解。”

J.B 16/4

REPORT
Date April 16, 1937.
Subject "Literary Arts Society of China - alleged anti-Japanese
activities.
Made by D.S. McKeown    Forwarded by J. Boyne A S I

On April 15, 1937, the Nichi-Nichi, a local Japanese
newspaper, published an article (translation attached) entitled
"Chinese Cultural Society commits lese majeste" in which it
is stated that Hung Sun and Fu Tong Hwa are reported to have
organized a Chinese Cultural Society in order to develop an
anti-Japanese movement. The article continues by asserting
that recently the society published a pamphlet entitled
"Records of National Crisis" written by one Dong Tseng Hwa
(董振華) and a poem published on the ninth page of the
pamphlet contains an expression which constitutes lese
majeste against the Emperor of Japan.

Extracts from the pamphlet which may be considered
objectionable have been translated and are attached.

Enquiries show that the pamphlet in question was written
and published by one Dong Tseng Hwa. The first edition appeared
in April 1936 and the second edition in June of the same year.
The sole agency for this book is the Life Reading Society
(生活書社), 71 Love Lane, Bubbling Well Road, which in turn
distributed the books to various books stores on Foochow Road
for sale.

According to the employees of the Life Reading Society
the transaction which authorized the Society to be the sole
agent of the book in question was made between the author and
Li Kung Poh (李公樸), who is now under detention in the Kiangsu
High Court at Soochow awaiting for trial, consequently none of
the present staff of the Society have any knowledge regarding
the present whereabouts or antecedents of Dong Tseng Hwa.

1937年4月15日，本地日文报纸《日日新闻》刊登了一篇题为“中国文化协会犯大不敬罪”的文章（附译文），文中称据报洪深和傅东华组织了一个中国文化协会，以开展反日运动。文章接着断言，该会最近出版了一本由董振华（Dong Tseng Hwa）撰写的小册子，题为《国难记》，小册子第九页刊登的一首诗中含有构成对日本天皇大不敬的表述。

该小册子中可能被视为具有冒犯性的段落摘录已翻译并附后。

调查显示，涉案小册子由董振华撰写并出版。第一版于1936年4月问世，第二版于同年6月问世。该书的独家代理是位于静安寺路爱文义路71号的生活书社，该书社随后将书籍分发至福州路的各家书店销售。

据生活书社职员称，授权该社作为涉案书籍独家代理的交易是在作者与李公朴之间进行的，李公朴目前被拘押在苏州江苏高等法院候审，因此该社现任职员均不知晓董振华目前的下落或背景。

28 years of age and a native of Shanghai, adopted writing as
a hobby and is a merchant by profession dealing in general
goods. He is not a member of the Chinese Cultural Society
otherwise known as the Literary Arts Society of China.
Efforts to locate Dong Tseng Hwa have so far proved unsuccessful.
The Literary Arts Society of China (中國文藝協會) located
in Room 631, Continental Emporium Building, Nanking Road, was
formally inaugurated on March 28, 1937, at a meeting held in
the Chinese Y.M.C.A., 123 Boulevard de Montigny, when some **〔此处转录不清〕**
50 persons, including Mr. Chao Lih Ts (趙立士), Chief of the
Propaganda Department of the Central Kuomintang, Mr. Pan Kung
Chan, Chief of the Bureau of Social Affairs, and Mr. Doong
Ying Peh (董永伯) of the local Kuomintang, were present. Its
formation was reported to be sponsored by Mr. Pan Kung Chan,
Mr. Hung Sun and Mr. Fu Tong Hwa, professor of Chinan University,
together with a great number of well known authors and edu-
cationalists are its members.
Mr. Hung Sun, a dramatist and educationalist, was formerly
a director of the Star Motion Picture Company, and editor of
the Kwang Ming Magazine (光明). He was arrested in 1931
by the S.M.P. at the instance of the Chinese Authorities on
suspicion of being a communist but the charge against him was
dismissed. He is now in Canton.
Mr. Fu Tong Hwa, a textbook writer for the Commercial Press
and concurrently a professor of the Chinan University, resides
at No.6, Lane 342 Route Vallon, French Concession.
The report in the Nichi-Nichi is receiving the attention
of the Bureau of Social Affairs, a section chief of which
summoned one Zung Ta Chan (章達臣) of the Life Reading Society

二十八岁，上海人，以写作为业余爱好，职业为经营百货的商人。他不是中国文艺协会（又称中国文学艺术协会）的会员。
迄今为止，寻找董振华的努力均未成功。
中国文艺协会（中國文藝協會）位于南京路大陆商场631室，于1937年3月28日在莫利哀路123号中华基督教青年会举行的会议上正式成立，当时约有 **〔此处转录不清〕**
50人出席，包括国民党中央宣传部部长赵立士先生、社会局局长潘公展先生以及当地国民党党员董永伯先生。据报道，该会的成立由潘公展先生、洪深先生和暨南大学教授傅东华先生发起，众多知名作家和教育家为其会员。
洪深先生是一位剧作家和教育家，曾任明星电影公司导演及《光明》杂志编辑。他于1931年应中国当局要求，因涉嫌为共产党员而被上海公共租界工部局警务处逮捕，但针对他的指控后被撤销。他目前在广州。
傅东华先生是商务印书馆的教科书编写者，同时兼任暨南大学教授，居住在法租界华伦路342弄6号。
《日日新闻》的报道正受到社会局的关注，该局一名科长传讯了生活书社的章达臣

Subject (in full).... Anti-Japanese Publication entitled "Records of National Crisis".

Made by.... and .... Forwarded by.... Supt.. Tan Shao Liang.

Dr. Hung Chi telephoned this afternoon stating that the Police Bureau has received a complaint from the Japanese Consulate-General to the effect that a booklet entitled "Records of National Crisis" obtainable in book stores in Shanghai contains highly objectionable articles against the Japanese and requested that its circulation be suppressed.

Dr. Hung Chi, apart from transmitting this information, will write officially to the Commissioner of Police.

page_data.en:
Translation of a song contained in Page 9 of a booklet
entitled "Record of National Crisis".
----------
We should not be willing to cast aside our riches and
honour, glory and prosperity;
we have to think of some way to keep them.
The labourers and peasants in the islands have already been
sucked of all their blood,
The only way out for us is to carry out the continental policy.
The mainland of China is our life line;
It has all kinds of products,
And there are millions of toiling labourers and peasants,
whose blood will last a long time for us to suck;
The last Emperor pointed out this way long ago,
Along which we have to march from three directions;
The first was to conquer Formosa,
The second was to get Korea into our possession,
The third step was to occupy Manchuria and Mongolia;
Even these are not yet enough,
The whole of China must be devoured,
before the third step can be said completely finished;
When China has been totally occupied,
The conquest of the whole world will then follow.
The first and the second steps had been taken already,
It is time for us to come to the third step.
When the X X Emperor read this petition,
His mind was so happy that he granted permission;
The Emperor has really no power in his hands,
The capitalists have the power in their possession.
The capitalists have money so they have power,
Militarists and officials are only their running dogs;
page_data.zh:
题为《国难记》的小册子第9页所载歌曲的译文。
---
我们不应愿意抛弃我们的财富和
荣誉、光荣与繁荣；
我们必须想办法保持它们。
岛屿上的劳工和农民已被吸干了鲜血，
我们唯一的出路是执行大陆政策。
中国大陆是我们的生命线；
它拥有各种产品，
还有数百万勤劳的劳工和农民，
他们的鲜血足够我们吸取很长时间；
先皇早已指出这条道路，
我们必须从三个方向沿此进军；
第一步是征服台湾，
第二步是将朝鲜纳入我们的版图，
第三步是占领满洲和蒙古；
即使这些还不够，
必须吞并整个中国，
才能说第三步完全完成；
当中国被完全占领时，
征服全世界也将随之而来。
第一步和第二步已经采取，
现在是我们进行第三步的时候了。
当 XX 天皇读到这份奏折时，
他心中非常高兴并予以批准；
天皇手中其实没有权力，
权力掌握在资本家手中。
资本家有钱所以有权，
军阀和官员只是他们的走狗；

page_data.en:

The X X capitalists are blood-sucking devils,
Year after year they become richer and richer than ever.
The capitalists and militarists make a wicked plot,
For the occupation of China.
As they had influence in the North-East,
The 4 North-Eastern provinces were the first to be seized.

年复一年，他们变得比以往更加富有。
资本家和军阀策划邪恶阴谋，
旨在占领中国。
由于他们在东北拥有影响力，
东北四省首先被夺取。
